+# Incident Postmortem: High P99 Latency on booklogr-api
+
+## Root Cause
+Commit 69df4ff ("Schema cleanup: drop unused books title index") introduced migration e2a9d4c1b6f8_drop_unused_books_title_index.py, which dropped the composite index ix_books_owner_lower_title on books(owner_id, lower(title)).
+However, the GET /v1/books endpoint in api/routes/books.py defaults to querying Books.query.filter(Books.owner_id == claim_id) sorted by func.lower(Books.title). Without the index, every request for the default library listing required a full table scan and sort across user books, elevating p99 request latency above 500ms and triggering the BooklogrApiLatencyP99High Prometheus alert.
+
+## Key Evidence Used
+1. Firing Prometheus alert BooklogrApiLatencyP99High: p99 HTTP request latency on booklogr-api exceeded the 300ms threshold (measured ~500-700ms).
+2. Prometheus query histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, path) (rate(flask_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))) pinpointed /v1/books as the slow endpoint.
+3. Code in api/routes/books.py (get_books()) showed filtering on claim_id and sorting on func.lower(Books.title).
+4. Git commit history (git log -n 5) showed recent commit 69df4ff ("Schema cleanup: drop unused books title index") which removed ix_books_owner_lower_title.
+
+## Changes Made
+Created database migration migrations/versions/f3b2a1c4d5e6_restore_books_owner_title_index.py to restore the composite index ix_books_owner_lower_title on books(owner_id, lower(title)).
